newsitem.title: SPAIN: N.Ireland minister sees Basque, Irish parallels.
newsitem.headline: N.Ireland minister sees Basque, Irish parallels.

text.p: A senior British official said on Wednesday there were parallels between the conflicts in Northern Ireland and Spain's Basque country, with a "culture of violence" in both that had to be overcome.

Michael Ancram, junior minister for the British-ruled province, told a news conference in the Basque town of Vitoria that the majority in both societies rejected violence, but a minority still had to be weaned away from it.
"In both places there has to be a departure from violence in order to get those that defend it involved in a process of negotiation and peace," Ancram said.
"As members of democratic governments, we have a joint interest in solving these problems in a democratic manner," he added referring to the Madrid and London governments.
The IRA (Irish Republican Army) is fighting to end British rule in Northern Ireland, while ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) is fighting for Basque independence from Spain.
Ancram said the government and people of Britain were still willing for multi-party peace talks to include the IRA's political arm Sinn Fein "once the ceasefire was restored".
"They accept conversations tied to peace, but they will never accept that this process develops as blackmail, under pressure," he said.
The IRA abandoned a 17-month truce in February last year and set off a string of bombs in London.

The minister was making the visit to discuss political and economic developments in Northern Ireland and to tap into the considerable Spanish interest in the region, the British embassy in Madrid said.
Ancram met Basque leaders early on Wednesday and was to dine with Spanish Interior Minister Jaime Mayor Oreja later.
